Header: Podosphaera spp. Powdery mildew; Bungabunga in Bemba

Prevention: Remove weeds and residues in areas with powdery mildew history, as they may harbour the disease, and bury them far from the cultivated field.
Crop-rotate with cereals, onion or garlic to break the disease cycle.
Do not plant a nursery near the old diseased crop
Spray a preventive fungicide in the rainy season if you had mildew problems in the previous year.
Refer to direct control yellow column.
Monitoring: Powdery mildew is a fungal disease and a problem in the dry and hot season.
During the initial stage check for fine dusty whitish powdery fungal growth on the leaves 3 weeks after germination.
When severe, leaves become yellow or dried and brownish.
Monitor weekly when the crop is still young and at least once every two weeks when the crop is maturing.
Action should be taken when 6-10 out of 100 plants are showing the initial spots of thin green-whitish powder spots on upper leaves.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Prune heavily diseased leaves (bury at least 30 cm) to reduce spread of disease
Pound 1.5kg of neem leaves and soak them in 16 litres of water for 24 hours.
Sieve the mixture, add 50g of soft soap like
SunlightTM and spray once per week but no later than 10-14 days before harvest.
Use baking soda (potassium bicarbonate) mix 2.5 tablespoons of baking soda with 2.5 tablespoons of vegetable oil in 16 litres of water, add 2.5 teaspoons of soft soap like
LifebuoyTM as a sticker and stir.
Spray on the leaves once in 2 weeks.
Repeat if new infested plants occur.
Use 9-10 tablespoons vinegar mixed with 16 litres of water and spray every 2 weeks

Restrictions
Most fungicides are protective and thus reduce or prevent new infestation.
They cannot usually cure an infested plant.
If whitish powder is seen everywhere, treatments are too late.
When using a pesticide (even a botanical home-brew), always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (ZEMA).
